questions.text: Define an Embedded System. Explain the characteristics and constraints of embedded systems (Real-time operation, low power consumption, tight memory footprint, cost, environmental robustness). Compare Microprocessor vs Microcontroller vs System-on-Chip (SoC).

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Embedded System Architecture & Core Hardware Components
questions.text: Explain the ARM Cortex-M Architecture (Cortex-M3/M4). Describe the Register set, Nested Vectored Interrupt Controller (NVIC), Memory Map, and Thumb-2 Instruction Set.

Explain the significance of `volatile`, `const`, and `static` keywords in Embedded C programming with practical microcontroller register manipulation examples. Explain bitwise operations in C for setting, clearing, and toggling specific GPIO pins.

Differentiate between General Purpose OS (GPOS) vs Real-Time OS (RTOS), Hard Real-Time vs Soft Real-Time systems. Explain RTOS Kernel services: Tasks, Task States (Ready, Running, Blocked, Suspended), Context Switching, and Task Control Block (TCB).

Explain Real-Time Scheduling Algorithms: (a) Rate Monotonic Scheduling (RMS - Static priority), and (b) Earliest Deadline First (EDF - Dynamic priority). Derive Liu and Layland's utilization bound for RMS: $U = \sum \frac{C_i}{T_i} \le n(2^{1/n} - 1)$. Test the schedulability of 3 periodic tasks under RMS and EDF.

Explain Priority Inversion in RTOS. How does priority inversion cause deadlocks/starvation in mission-critical systems (e.g. Mars Pathfinder)? Explain solutions: (a) Priority Inheritance Protocol (PIP), and (b) Priority Ceiling Protocol (PCP).

Compare Serial Communication Protocols used in embedded systems: UART, SPI, and I2C in terms of wiring lines, master/slave operation, data rate, transmission distance, and synchronization. Draw the I2C bus timing diagram showing START condition, 7-bit Address, R/W bit, ACK/NACK, Data byte, and STOP condition with pull-up resistors.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Hardware-Software Co-Design, Low-Power Design & Embedded System Debugging
questions.text: Explain the Hardware-Software Co-Design methodology in embedded systems design. Explain Debugging and Testing techniques: In-Circuit Emulators (ICE), JTAG (IEEE 1149.1 boundary scan), Serial Wire Debug (SWD), and Watchdog Timers (WDT).

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Embedded System Architecture & Core Hardware Components
questions.text: Explain Memory Types in embedded systems: SRAM, DRAM, Flash ROM, EEPROM, and FRAM. Explain the Memory Map of an embedded program: Text (.text), Data (.data), BSS (.bss), Heap, and Stack segments.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Embedded System Architecture & Core Hardware Components
questions.text: Explain Controller Area Network (CAN) Bus protocol in automotive and industrial embedded systems. Explain CAN differential signaling ($CAN_H, CAN_L$), Non-Destructive Bitwise Arbitration using message identifiers, and frame formats.
